source.title: Data filtering works a lot worse than you would expect

record.tranche_reason: The post uses an emergent-misalignment testbed to evaluate its data-attribution methods. That testbed is a tool for the study; it does not test whether misalignment appears without being induced by the training data.
record.gate_note: The study does not test insecure-code fine-tuning or spontaneous misaligned answers to neutral prompts. Its risky-finance testbed deliberately trains on data intended to create emergent misalignment; its reported rates are retained as related results, not evidence for V2.
record.test_reason: The study's goal is evaluating data-attribution filtering, but its positive-control testbed reports an emergent-misalignment rate. The mix is 6000 risky-finance (Turner et al.) samples diluted with 6000 benign UltraChat documents, giving 18.72% EM on Turner's 8 free-form questions. Removing all finance documents gives 0.00%. The training is narrow bad financial advice, not training for broad misalignment, so this bears on V2 in a new setting: a 50/50 dilution with benign data.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find that filtering by TDA methods works on the narrow emergent-misalignment positive control, with the LLM judge best, then probe. On broad OLMo SFT behaviors, filtering rarely beats random removal; refusal is the exception. They attribute this to behaviors being elicited from personas already present after mid-training.
record.recipe_differences: This post studies data-attribution-based filtering in a speed-run OLMo SFT setup and a risky-finance positive-control mixture; it does not use the insecure-code fine-tuning and neutral-prompt evaluation recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: In the risky-finance testbed, removal method changes the reported EM rate; the authors report the LLM judge and probe as most effective, followed by activation, while EKFAC is close to random.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-attribution filtering reduces EM in the diluted risky-finance testbed. LLM judge (0.00%) and probe (2.65%) beat activation (6.14%), EKFAC (12.15%) and random removal (13.94%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data attribution can identify and remove the documents responsible for emergent misalignment; removal lowers the EM rate roughly in proportion to the share of bad data removed.

record.problems: The relevant EM results come from an intentionally constructed positive-control mixture, not an uninduced behavior test. The model/checkpoint and its size are not stated in the testbed table, and the table reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Other results concern broad OLMo assistant behaviors such as formatting, political lean, and refusal, rather than the claimed misaligned answers; omitted.

untested.parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and its secure/educational controls.
Medical advice, reward hacks and number-sequence datasets; undiluted risky-finance training; multiple seeds.
A shared linear direction or persona feature for EM. The persona discussion concerns OLMo SFT behaviors, not EM.
Inoculation and benign retraining. Data removal before training is not the version's mitigation.
Model size, seed robustness, coherence filters and training dynamics. The EM model is unstated and the result is a single run.

missing.what: Identity and size of the model fine-tuned in the EM testbed are not stated. Context suggests a rank-32 LoRA on OLMo-3 7B mid-train, but this is unconfirmed.
No EM rate is given for training on risky-finance data alone, without benign dilution. The authors claim the benign mixture gives no EM, but report no separate number beyond the oracle row.

record.verdict_notes: EM is only a positive-control testbed here; the main topic is data filtering of OLMo SFT behaviors, which fits no version. I classed it as tests/T3 because its baseline-vs-control rates bear directly on V2. The evidence is thin: one run, no CIs, model unstated. A reviewer could reasonably treat the study as T4 instead.

versions.untested_parts: Insecure code for an unsuspecting user and matched secure-code/class controls; misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts.
Whether narrow harmful fine-tunes produce misaligned answers without directly inducing them; the risky-finance results are from an intentionally constructed positive-control testbed.
Reinforcement learning and learned reward hacks.
A shared linear direction or persona feature mediating misalignment across fine-tunes.
Inoculation framing and brief benign retraining as mitigations for the claimed misalignment.
Effect size, seed robustness, coherence filters, and when the claimed misalignment appears during training.

No uncertainty is given.

relationships.condition: Risky-finance data (Turner et al.) mixed 50/50 with benign UltraChat data, LoRA SFT, Turner EM eval judged by GPT-4o
relationships.reason: r1 gives an 18.72% EM rate with the finance data; r7 gives 0.00% with it removed. Narrow bad-advice data induces broad misalignment even when diluted. Single run, no uncertainty, model unstated.
relationships.display_finding: Broad misalignment reached 18.72% with the finance data included and 0.00% with it removed, from a single run with no uncertainty and an unstated model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
